h: Harrow's Hidden History, and How to Win at Crazy Golf
p: A few crazy golf tips to give you the edge. Don't just whack the ball as hard as you can. Most holes reward a gentle touch, especially around the ramps and obstacles. Look at the angles before you putt, as banking the ball off a wall is often the clever way round. And keep a sense of humour, because the course is designed to throw in a few cheeky bounces when you least expect them.

For families, let the younger ones putt first and give them a bit of help lining up their shots. Little wins keep them happy all the way round. If you're playing with older kids or friends, keep a scorecard and agree a prize for the winner (or a forfeit for whoever comes last).

Once you've finished, there's plenty of history to explore around Harrow. The famous hilltop village of Harrow on the Hill is home to Harrow School, where former pupils include Winston Churchill and Lord Byron. In the churchyard of St Mary's Church, at the very top of the hill, is the Peachey tomb, where Byron is said to have sat and written poetry as a schoolboy, enjoying the views over the surrounding countryside.

Back down the hill, Headstone Manor and Museum is a fascinating spot to visit, with a moated manor house dating back to the Middle Ages and exhibitions on Harrow's history. It's surrounded by a pleasant park, ideal for a picnic. And if you're a football or music fan, Wembley Stadium is just a short trip away, easy to reach by Tube or train from Harrow. With so much on the doorstep, a round of crazy golf can easily become a full day out.
